$comment: SPLIT MANIFEST — reserved families are declared HERE, BEFORE any discovery run, and are never reassigned to sealed_eval after results are seen. Moving a family requires opening a documented change with a reason and a date, and reporting results under both assignments. An inclusion-only manifest is not a manifest.
partition_rule: Partition by FAMILY, not by row. Hash-based splitting is a backstop, not a mechanism: near-duplicate tasks and variant templates leak across hash boundaries constantly because they differ in surface form while testing identical capability.
held_out_attacker_rule: A renamed or reprompted training FM is NOT an unseen attacker. Attacker identity is the claim under test. If a candidate held-out FM shares a generator lineage, prompt, or template with any training FM, the evaluation measures recall of the training distribution rather than transfer.

sealed_eval.purpose: Transfer measurement. Evaluated once, after the selection policy is frozen.
sealed_eval.$note: MUST contain at least one FM family and one attack template that appear in no other split. An empty sealed_eval means the primary hypothesis is untestable.

dev.purpose: Infrastructure, prompts, and smoke tests. Not a measurement surface.

integrity_checks: Every family and template appears in exactly one split.
sealed_eval contains at least one FM family absent from all other splits.
No task family in sealed_eval appears in any other split.
Near-duplicate detection has run across splits BEFORE fine-tuning.
frozen is true before any fine-tuning run begins.
